G4_guess_resistance.trials_note: 20,000 structure-aware trials here plus 10,000 in the final sweep, 0 hits in 30,000 total. Below the 200k the contract asks for, but not load-bearing: the EXACT enumeration at easy gives a density of 1.4e-7 directly, and the family is rejected on H, not on G4.

G5_density_and_cost.fail_reason: the strongest attack SOLVES the shipping preset 40/40 in a median of 35 nodes and 0.22 s; a large space and a low density are not difficulty
G5_density_and_cost.shipping_density_basis: exact enumeration at easy (m=n=5): 1-2 valid answers out of 6,935,760 standard bitableaux of admissible shape; at demo (m=n=4) the exact counts are 1,2,3,19
G5_density_and_cost.strongest_attack: constraint propagation on the forced row multisets (shape forced by Lemma 7.22; row content forced by the multiplicity-wise union; R and C decouple)

G6_adversary_panel.fail_reason: two of the four attacks succeed, one of them with no search at all; Track B requires a FAILING in-context attack and there is none

G8_canonical_key.invariance_note: the key is invariant under swapping f and g, which is the family's only relabelling symmetry (indices are not permutable: the term order of Definition 7.6 is not symmetric under relabelling rows or columns)

certificate_language.description: A standard bitableau over [m]x[n]: an ordered list of minors (S_j|T_j) with |S_j|=|T_j| non-increasing in j, each S_j a strictly increasing subset of [m] and T_j of [n], such that both the row and the column tableau are semi-standard.

compact_route.name: constraint propagation on the forced row multisets (shape forced by Lemma 7.22, row content forced by the multiplicity-wise union, R and C decouple)

hidden_term_order_idea.measurement: toric ideals, from-scratch Buchberger over Q, weight order tie-broken by lex, 250 random weight vectors per instance
hidden_term_order_idea.reason_1: not this paper's mathematics: the bideterminant term order (Definition 7.6) is a single fixed order, and a Robbiano-style weight characterisation of pseudo-ASL term orders is the paper's Open Question 10.4
hidden_term_order_idea.reason_2: the valid answers form a full-dimensional Groebner cone (Mora-Robbiano 1988); recovering it is leading-term choice plus one LP

mechanical_route.basis: exact count via the hook-content formula: #standard bitableaux of shape lambda over [m]x[n] = s_{lambda'}(1^m) * s_{lambda'}(1^n)
mechanical_route.name: the paper's Algorithm 7.1 (get-admissible-shapes + get-admissible-standard-bd + line-10 divisibility filter)

paper_error_found.claim: Theorem 7.19 completeness: every least common standard multiple has exactly P = max_i max(rd_i, cd_i) columns; get-admissible-shapes returns only such shapes
paper_error_found.consequence: leastness has no cheap closed-form certificate; verify() must enumerate the one-column-smaller divisors
paper_error_found.reason: P ignores the shape-containment constraint lambda contains shape(f) union shape(g); here that union is (2,1), already two columns
paper_error_found.second_error: the worked example in applications.tex lists 12 bitableaux as LCM(f,g); f lt-divides none of the three shape-(3,3,2) ones checked. It shows the unfiltered line-9 output. Under the algorithm as written the answer is 3, all of shape (3,2,2).

problem_profile.hardness_basis: REJECTED.  Track B was the only candidate and it fails: the compact route IS an in-context attack.  Constraint propagation over the forced row multisets solves 40/40 shipping instances in a median of 34 backtracking nodes (~5e2 exact operations, 0.14 s), and a zero-search padding heuristic solves 6/8.  The paper's own Algorithm 7.1 enumerates ~7e6 standard bitableaux at the same preset, but that gap is not testable because the short side is trivially reachable by hand.
problem_profile.intuition_description: Row i of every common multiple must contain the multiplicity-wise union of row i of f and row i of g, and the shape must contain the multiset union of the two shapes; a solver who does not see this must search standard bitableaux.
native_objects: bideterminants (products of minors) of a generic matrix
